title: Oliver band reception and changing audiences for jazz
summary: Oliver's band was good but not extraordinary; the public then was not yet taken with Dixieland, unlike now.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You of course heard a lot of King Oliver and Freddie Keppard, and of course Louis Armstrong, all of those New Orleans trumpet players, so many great ones that I don't know which one you can pick. Oh yes, there are a lot of
new fellas now, I don't know these boys only by reputation who are, the boys who are with Basie and Duke, oh those boys are just
wonderful, marvelous. Yeah they have a lot of technique and range, but I still don't think they have quite a tone. Oh my yeah, but it brings us back to what we were
speaking in the beginning, those boys have had fine training, fine schooling.
Can you remember much about the Oliver band when they were here? Well they were pretty much
on the same order of the average Dixieland outfit, they were all very good, but I wouldn't say nothing too extraordinary.

I wondered about their reception, of course the people like myself are more or less a fanatic on the New Orleans style of music, and to me they were so wonderful, just to hear them on the record, what's left. And I wasn't here in those days to hear them, but did they go over unusually well? I mean, did they have the general public or was it just the

certainly the cafe? No, no, no, not at that time. The public hadn't taken to the to the Dixieland idea of music. Of course the music lovers who like that type of thing, they went for it. But not as popular as it is now. You take now, you take these young colleges, these young boys who are in colleges now, my gosh, they go all out for that type of thing. And even having these fellas lecture in these colleges. Duke, Duke has lectured at Yale, at Harvard, all these fine institutions. Look what's happening at Ravinia. Lionel Hampton is on the bill there. Earl Garner is on the bill there. Those things were unheard of years ago.
That's right. But I wondered if the general public, or if it was just the small group, I know it wasn't just the South Side.
It's the general public if you judge from the attendance.
